runs.name: MSC Industrial Direct Co., Inc.
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$128.67** (close 2026-10-12, `tools/run.py` live quote, aggregator, flagged). Shares **55,846,298** Class A, one class (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-05-30, acc 0001003078-26-000080, cover as of 2026-06-17; issued less treasury 55,846,186, within 112 shares; the Class B reclassified into Class A at 1.225 for 1 in Q1 FY2024); cap **$7,186M**. Sovereign **5.60%** (USD; US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (year ended 2025-08-30, filed 2025-10-23, acc 0001003078-25-000123), 10-Ks FY2024 (0001003078-24-000107), FY2023 (0001003078-23-000102), FY2021 (0001003078-21-000199), FY2017 (0001003078-17-000307), the 10-Q above, the proxy DEF 14A of 2025-12-11 (0001003078-25-000174), 8-Ks including the RPA amendment (0001003078-25-000181), the new chief executive from 2026-01-01 (0001003078-26-000006) and the new chief financial officer from 2026-09-14 (0001003078-26-000094); the FY2026 10-K not yet filed. One figure cross-checked: FY2025 operating cash $333,717 thousand filed, equal to the tagged figure. Ten balance sheets read in Step 0. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (margin and cost over full cycles against rivals; volume against price; the receivables purchase agreement; the 2023 Class B reclassification and the buybacks after it; the balance sheets). Competitors: the 10-K names no rival, only classes of rival; the analyst took the three SEC filers in MRO supply from the filer's own proxy peer group (W.W. Grainger, Fastenal, Global Industrial) and said so; web sellers, warehouse stores and manufacturers' sales forces not compared, flagged. **Q1 IN**: one segment, a distributor of metalworking and MRO supplies whose economics (volume tied to industrial production, gross margin, operating cost per sales dollar, working capital) can be pictured ten years out from its own and its rivals' filings. **Q2 OUT**: the castle shown narrowing on the evidence over three cycles: operating margin 17.5% (FY2012) to 8.0% (FY2025), cycle peaks 17.5%, 13.1%, 12.1%, while Grainger went 12.6% to 13.9% and Fastenal held about 20%; operating cost per sales dollar 28.3 cents to 32.8 cents, from the lowest of the three to the highest (Grainger 25.2, Fastenal 24.8); gross margin 45.8% to 40.8%, each step explained by the filer as pricing and mix, a FY2024 "web price realignment initiative" and a strategy to "adjust our customer pricing to maintain competitiveness"; volume down about $191M net over FY2023 to FY2025; sales +60% over the span with about $817M of purchased businesses against Grainger +100% and Fastenal +162%; the latest quarter's 10.2% margin came from price ($70.1M) not volume ($4.5M) and is not credited, one quarter not being a full cycle. Q3 to Q12 not reached; no research pass. After the stop, recorded not weighed: a $300M receivables sale in FY2023 under the RPA, raised to $350M in December 2025, derecognised, covenants the credit facility's, putting $300M into FY2023's operating cash; restructuring charges every year; equity flat for a decade ($1.10B to $1.42B) while retained earnings fell $1,040M to $433M; goodwill and intangibles 33% of assets; net debt $432.7M at 2026-05-30 plus the $350M RPA; a repurchase plan with no price named; integrity facts recorded, not judged: the family's Class B exchanged at 1.225 Class A each (about 1.95M more shares than one-for-one), then $187.7M bought back in FY2024 partly to offset that dilution and funded by borrowing, two board nominees for the family, the family chief executive's FY2025 cash bonus $1,425,750 in a year operating income fell 22.8%. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: window FY2021 to FY2025, trough to trough, the literal window the cycle base; owner cash after all spending (stock pay, capital spending, purchases, finance leases, working capital, the one-time $300M RPA inflow removed) average $198.1M; maintenance case (depreciation as the guess) $240.6M; growth cut by specific (f) from 15.2% to the business's own sales growth of 3.83%; range **$74.08 to $84.75 a share** all-equity against $128.67 (equity-only $76.94 to $85.87; RPA counted as debt $70.03 to $81.49); floor tested first, no case earns it at the price (most generous case 4.6%); fair price beneath the stop **$39.99 all-equity**, $44.59 equity-only, $35.16 with the RPA as debt; not armed (box not OUT at Q7). The analyst confessed one CONVENTION of this run: the RPA treated as working capital by extension of Q7's inventory-secured trade finance convention, the debt-counted figures beside. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing showing seven other 2026-10-13 file names (none MSM), the session's starting commit subjects, the memory index's project-state lines; none opened or used. Commits 89a34a4e, 99ee49c6, 92c8c4f8, 44699eed. Citations: the analyst's check PASS (43 ids, 0 bad); the dispatcher's script (`dispatcher_check.py`) found every id in the ledger and no E-id; its 20 unmatched hits are filing quotations sharing a paragraph with ids and, beside L1995-023, the row's own words ("lost a notch"), 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) neither the framework nor the template says where to take rivals when the 10-K names none; a pay peer group is not the filer's statement of who it competes with; (2) Q7's net-debt definition leaves out a receivables facility treated as a sale but covenanted like debt, and nothing says what to do with the one-time operating-cash inflow when such a facility starts; a ruling would make factoring companies' runs comparable; (3) the framework has no test separating a castle that "has lost still another notch" (L1995-023) from one filled in on the evidence, and another analyst could weigh this record TOO HARD (NATURE); the computation makes the choice moot at this price. The analyst could not trace the FY2019 and FY2020 falls in retained earnings, cross-check the peers' tagged margins to their filed statements, or compare the unnamed web rivals.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a metalworking and MRO distributor whose castle is shown narrowing over three cycles: operating margin 17.5% to 8.0% while Grainger rose and Fastenal held about 20%, operating cost per sales dollar moved from the lowest of the three to the highest, gross margin cut by pricing against transparent web rivals, volume down about $191M over FY2023 to FY2025; Q1 IN. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range $74.08 to $84.75 a share all-equity against $128.67, no case earns the floor (best 4.6%); fair $39.99 all-equity ($44.59 equity-only), not armed. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: the family's Class B exchanged at 1.225 for 1 and the dilution bought back with borrowed money; a $350M receivables sale facility outside debt on the face.
